answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each account to lock scarce tokens before it can vote on reputation or claim rewards, then slash that stake when independent audits show fabricated work. The lock makes identities costly rather than free: splitting one agent into a hundred accounts does not create more voting weight without a hundred times the capital. A prism of audit signals can expose copied outputs; a raven-like monitor flags suspicious account clusters, while zenith marks the minimum stake threshold. The attacker risks losing real funds, not merely disposable identities.
